arguments.name: Tasker Layout
arguments.description:
Will show the text in a custom Tasker toast instead of using a normal system toast.

You can use HTML to format your text when this option is enabled. For example, you can use <font color=red>Some Text</font> to show some text in red.

Useful to get advanced toast functionality or if your device doesn't support multi-line toasts for example.

arguments.name: Title
arguments.description: Title to show up above the normal toast text. If not set, only the text will show.

arguments.name: Icon
arguments.description:
Icon to show on the toast.

If not set, no icon will be shown at all.

arguments.name: Icon Size
arguments.description:
Size of the icon in dip (density-independent pixels).

Default value is 24.

arguments.name: Background Colour
arguments.description:
Color for the background of the toast.

If not set the current Tasker theme background color will be used.

arguments.name: Task
arguments.description:
If set, will make the toast interactive and when clicked will call the chosen task.

All the variables available in the task where the toast is created will also be available in the called task.

arguments.name: Timeout
arguments.description:
Time in milliseconds the toast should appear on the screen.

If set Will override the normal 'Long' setting above.

arguments.name: Continue Task Immediately
arguments.description: If disabled, will not advance the task to the next action until the toast is gone from the screen.

arguments.name: Text Colour
arguments.description:
Color for the text of the toast.

If not set, an appropriate text color for the background color will be chosen so that it has good contrast.

If HTML is used in the text and color is sent that way, it'll override this setting just for those parts of the text.

arguments.name: Dismiss On Click
arguments.description: If enabled, will make the flash go away as soon as it's clicked and the task is launched.

arguments.name: Show Over Everything
arguments.description:
If enabled, will make the toast show over system UI like the notification tray, lock screen, or even AOD on some devices.

Tasker's accessibility service needs to be on for this to work.

If you want you can disable the 'Continue Task Immediately' option and Tasker will toggle the service on and off when needed automatically.

arguments.name: Position
arguments.description:
One of TopLeft, Top, TopRight, Right, BottomRight, Bottom, BottomLeft or Left.

Can optionally provide an offset in dip separated by a comma from the position.

Use the helper for easier setup.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description:
If you set an ID and an existing flash is already showing with the same ID, it'll be replaced by the new one.

If no ID is set, they will appear on top of each other.

arguments.name: Ignore DND
arguments.description: If enabled, will not try to restore the active DND mode after changing the sound mode

arguments.name: Prompt If Not Granted
arguments.description: If any of the permissions above are not granted yet, a dialog will show before asking for the permissions to explain why they're needed.

arguments.name: Mime Type
arguments.description:
You can change the mimetype of the uploaded file and Google will automatically try to convert the file to that type.

For example, you can upload a Microsoft Excel file with the Google Sheets mimetype and the uploaded file will be a usable Google Sheets file.

Some types are not compatible with the uploaded data and in those cases Google Drive will respond with a 'Bad Request' error.

arguments.name: Text/SSML
arguments.description:
You can either use normal text or SSML.

Normal text will automatically try to create natural sounding intonations for your sentences.

SSML will allow you to very precisely control how your sentences are generated.

Learn more about SSML by clicking the button below.

arguments.name: Headers
arguments.description:
Query Parameters (Format: key1:value1
key2:value2... - Same format as Headers)

arguments.name: From
arguments.description:
The start time for your data query in milliseconds since the Jan 1, 1970, 00:00:00.000 GMT (epoch time).

This input determines the start point of the period you want to look up.

arguments.name: To
arguments.description:
The end time for your data query in milliseconds since the Jan 1, 1970, 00:00:00.000 GMT (epoch time).

You can use the %TIMEMS variable to look up data until right now.

arguments.name: Package
arguments.description: If empty, the data for the whole device will be gotten and not just a specific app or apps

arguments.name: Image
arguments.description: Setting an image on the clipboard will overwrite the text above

arguments.name: Is Sensitive Data
arguments.description: If enabled, will not show the text or image you set on the clipboard in the system clipboard overlay

arguments.name: Force High Accuracy
arguments.description: If enabled will force Tasker to use GPS to get your location and will not use other location getting methods at all

arguments.name: Convert Orientation
arguments.description: If enabled will convert orientation values to degrees. Result must have at least 3 values for this to work.

arguments.name: Mode
arguments.description:
You can either start, stop or query a screen capture.

Starting a capture when it's already started will result in an error.

Stopping a capture when it's already stopped will result in an error.

Use 'Query' to know if a capture is currently ongoing or not (check the %sc_is_capturing variable).

arguments.name: Video Encoder
arguments.description: Will be H264 by default.

arguments.name: Resolution
arguments.description: Will use your screen's resolution by default

arguments.name: Video Bitrate
arguments.description:
The higher the bitrate, the less pixelated will the final video look.

Not all bitrates may be supported by all devices.

If not manually set, will be 5000000.

arguments.name: Video Framerate
arguments.description:
The higher the framerate, the smoother the recorded video's motion will be.

If not manually set, will be 30.

arguments.name: Enable Debugging (Check Help)
arguments.description:
Most people don't need debugging to be enabled at all times on their Android devices. It might be a security risk if you accidentally accept an unknown request to start debugging which could put your phone at risk.

By enabling this option you can leave debugging off and the action will enable it when ran and disable it afterwards, leaving your phone "closed down" for the majority of time!

arguments.name: Result Encoding
arguments.description:
If you are expecting a result with non-standard characters (like à or é) you can use a different encoding for the result.

Try using 'UTF-8' (no quotes) in situations like this, for example.

arguments.name: Image
arguments.description: If set, will show an image between the title and text

arguments.name: Max Width Or Height
arguments.description:
Size in dip (density-independent pixels). If an image is set you can optionally limit its size with this.

Original image proportions will always be respected.

arguments.name: Back Out
arguments.description: When enabled, will back out of the opened WhatsApp conversation so you end up where you were before the conversation was opened.

arguments.name: Local Variable Passthrough
arguments.description: If enabled all the variables that are available in this task will also be available in the parent task according to the restrictions below.

arguments.name: Replace On Passthrough
arguments.description:
If this is not enabled, variables that already have a value on the parent task will not be replaced by their values in this task.

Please note that you need to enable the option to allow replacements in the 'Perform Task' action as well.

arguments.name: Limit Passthrough To
arguments.description: If you only want to send a few variables back to the parent task, insert a / separated list of those variable names here.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: If you use the same id as an existing action it'll overwrite that action

arguments.name: Command
arguments.description:
The command sent will depend on the type of action:

- Button: just the command prefix

- Toggle: prefix=:=true_or_false (depending if toggled on or off)

- Range: prefix=:=current_value

- Toggle Range:prefix=:=true_or_false=:=current_value=:=mode (where mode is either 'toggle' or 'range' depending if you clicked the button or selected its range)

arguments.name: Disallow/Allow
arguments.description: Disallow to prevent call from going through. If you don't enable 'Reject', the caller will not know that you won't listen to the phone ring or vibrate. To them it'll seem like a normal call that is left unanswered.

arguments.name: Reject
arguments.description: Prevent call from going through and disconnects it as if the user had manually rejected it

arguments.name: Silence
arguments.description: Sets whether ringing should be silenced for the incoming call but call will still go through.

arguments.name: Skip Call Log
arguments.description: Prevent call from going through and make the call not appear in your call log

arguments.name: Skip Notification
arguments.description: Prevent call from going through make a missed call notification not shown for the incoming call

arguments.name: Names
arguments.description: One or more comma separated variable names

arguments.name: Variable Names Splitter
arguments.description:
Splitter for the variable names above.

By default is ',' or new line depending on what you use.

arguments.name: Values
arguments.description:
One or more values, each corresponding to the variable names above.

If more variable names than values exist, those variables will be unset.

arguments.name: Values Splitter
arguments.description:
Splitter for the values above.

By default is ',' or new line depending on what you use.

arguments.name: Do Maths
arguments.description: Will do maths on the values that support maths and leave the others as normal text

arguments.name: Keep Existing
arguments.description: Will only set the values of variables if they don't already exist by this point in the task

arguments.name: Type
arguments.description: One of the dialog types in the Tasker Input Dialog Types Catalog JSON. The "nd" (nameForDialogPickInput) field should be used here. Do NOT use the "i" or "n" fields. For example, for a "Yes or No" dialog type, use "YesOrNo" and NOT "yn" or "Yes or No".

arguments.name: Title
arguments.description: If set will make a dialog appear prior to picking the input with the title and text, unless the specific input picker has a place for the title (like the Time dialog for example).

arguments.name: Text
arguments.description: Will appear in the dialog if the title is also set

arguments.name: Action
arguments.description:
Whether to show/update a progress dialog or to hide an existing one.

If you choose to hide the dialog but the dialog isn't showing the action will end successfully right away.

arguments.name: Title
arguments.description:
You must set this if the dialog isn't already showing.

If it's already showing you can omit this and the last used value will be kept.

arguments.name: Text
arguments.description:
You must set this if the dialog isn't already showing.

If it's already showing you can omit this and the last used value will be kept.

arguments.name: Type
arguments.description: You can either show a looping animation if you don't have a numeric progress to report, or show a progress bar where you can show numerical progress.

arguments.name: Animation Images
arguments.description: A list of images to use as an animation in the dialog.

arguments.name: Animation Tint
arguments.description:
This will tint the images with the selected color where they are not transparent.

By default this is set to Tasker's accent color

arguments.name: Frame Duration
arguments.description: The time in milliseconds that each image appears on the screen

arguments.name: Structure Type
arguments.description:
Select the type of data that the variable contains.

If the type doesn't match the data when being read then the type 'None' is assumed instead.

arguments.name: Prevent JSON Smart Search
arguments.description: If enabled, Tasker will not automatically search the full JSON structure for the value when reading it.

arguments.name: Names
arguments.description:
One or more array names, each on its line.

Each of these arrays will need to have the same number of values.

arguments.name: Joiner
arguments.description:
Will simply merge each position of the arrays above with the joiner.

For example, if you have 2 arrays, %names and %ages and use the joiner ' - ' it'll join '%names(1) - %ages(1)', '%names(2) - %ages(2)' and so on.

arguments.name: Format
arguments.description:
Will merge each position of the arrays above with the format you specify here.

Use the original array name as the placeholder in the format

For example, if you have 2 arrays, %names and %ages and use the fomat '%names is %ages years old' it'll join 
'%names(1) is %ages(1) years old'
'%names(2) is %ages(2) years old'
and so on.

arguments.name: Output
arguments.description:
Name of the array that will contain the formatted values.

Each position of this array will contain the corresponding positions of all the input arrays joined with the rules above.

arguments.name: Join Output
arguments.description: If set, will join the resulting array and make the output variable a single value instead of an array.

arguments.name: Replace Variables In Arrays
arguments.description: If enabled, Tasker will not only replace the array items themselves in, but it will look INSIDE those array items and replace any variables there too.

arguments.name: Output Variables
arguments.description:
Since the input supports both single values and arrays you can use any of these outputs as both single values and arrays.

The number of outputs will depend on how many dates are input.

Additionally, for each Output Format more results will be added for the formated output.

For example, if you have 2 inputs and 3 output formats, you'll get a total of 6 values in the formatted variable output.

arguments.name: Input
arguments.description:
One or more dates.

Can be direct values, values from variables or even direct arrays (use %array, not %array()).

arguments.name: Input Format
arguments.description:
One or more date formats.

For example, yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm will correctly parse a date like 2021/03/05 14:18

You can use a different format for each input.

If there are more inputs than formats, the last format on the list will be used for the remainder of the inputs.

arguments.name: Input Separator
arguments.description:
Separator will be comma or newline by default, depending if one of these characters is present in your text or not.

Set to a different separator manually if needed.

arguments.name: Output Format
arguments.description:
One or more date formats.

For example, yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm will produce a date like 2021/03/05 14:18

If you specify more than one output format, those formats will be applied to each input, so you'll have all the possible combinations of inputs and formats.

For example, if you have 2 inputs and 3 output formats, you'll get a total of 6 formatted values.

Check out all the possible formats below.

arguments.name: Output Format Separator
arguments.description:
Separator will be comma or newline by default, depending if one of these characters is present in your text or not.

Set to a different separator manually if needed.

arguments.name: Formatted Variable Names
arguments.description:
One or more variable names.

Each output will be directly mapped to the variable name available here, e.g., output 1 > variable name 1, output 2 > variable name 2, etc.

Special Behavior for the Last Variable Name:
If there are more output formats than variable names, the last variable name on this list gets special treatment:
1. It will hold its directly mapped output value (e.g., if it's the 2nd variable name, it gets the 2nd output).
2. An array using the same name (e.g., %varname()) will also be created.
 • The first element of this array (%varname(1)) will be the same directly mapped value mentioned above.
 • Any subsequent formatted outputs (those that didn't have their own dedicated variable name) will populate the rest of the array (e.g., %varname(2), %varname(3), etc.).

Example:

Suppose you have 3 Output Formats:
1. dd-MM-yy
2. d
3. yyyy

And 2 Formatted Variable Names:
1. %date
2. %index_day

For an input date of 03–06–25 (assuming input format dd–MM–yy):
• %date (Variable 1) will be: 03–06-25 (from Output Format 1).
• %index_day (Variable 2, the last variable name) will be: 3 (from Output Format 2).
• %index_day() (the array for the last variable name) will contain:
 • %index_day(1) = 3 (from Output Format 2)
 • %index_day(2) = 2025 (from Output Format 3, the remaining unmapped output)
So, %index_day() effectively becomes an array like [3, 2025].

arguments.name: Do Maths
arguments.description:
If enabled will allow you to do math operations in the 'Input' field only so that you can easily format dates in the past or future.

For example, %TIMES + 86400 (when used with the 'Seconds Since Epoch' input type) will format a date 1 day in the future (86400 seconds = 1 day).

arguments.name: Output Offset Type
arguments.description: If you want you can add seconds, minutes, hours or days to the output. This offset type will be applied to all outputs.

arguments.name: Output Offset
arguments.description:
The amount of offset for the type above.

Can be negative values.

You can use multiple offsets if you have more than one output.

arguments.name: Time Zone
arguments.description:
The time zone for the input time.

Useful if you want to format date/time for timezones other than the current one.

arguments.name: Regex
arguments.description:
A regex expression to match the input.

If you use group names in the regex expression Tasker will create a variable for each of those groups. That variable can be accessed either as direct value or as an array if multiple matches are found.

arguments.name: Match Pattern
arguments.description:
A regex expression to match the input.

If you use group names in the regex expression Tasker will create a variable for each of those groups. That variable can be accessed either as direct value or as an array if multiple matches are found.

arguments.name: Copy To Cache
arguments.description:
The URIs that the Android photo picker returns can only be used in Tasker so if you want to use the picked files with a third-party app (for example, with a Tasker plugin) you need to enable this option so that Tasker copies the files to cache and makes them usable on those third party apps.

Unfortunately this process will take longer for large files so please use only when really needed.

arguments.name: Pixel Coordinates
arguments.description:
X and Y coordinates in the 'x,y' format (no quotes), eg. to get the pixel color of the top-left most pixel in an image use 0,0.

You can specify multiple coordinates by putting each set of coordinates in a separate line.

You can use the % sign at the end of a coordinate to specify that coordinate in percentage relative to the image's size in that dimension.
For example, if you want to get the pixel color for the exact center of an image you can use the coordinates 50%,50%.

arguments.name: Only Monitor
arguments.description: Enable to only restart the Tasker monitor (like when you exit the app after making changes) and not fully restart Tasker.

arguments.name: Action
arguments.description:
The action to take on the services below.

The "…Keep Running" actions will change the general Tasker Setting available in Tasker > Menu > Preferences > Monitor > Keep Accessibility Running.

arguments.name: Services
arguments.description:
A comma separated list of accessibility services to act on with the action above.

Each service is represented by the app's package name followed by a "/" followed by the services class name.

arguments.name: Services
arguments.description:
A comma separated list of accessibility services to act on with the action above.

Each service is represented by the app's package name followed by a "/" followed by the services class name.

arguments.name: Get Cell Info
arguments.description: If checked, will request cell info directly from the modem (requires Android 10+). Returns the current cell ID, type, signal strength, and full cell info JSON.

output_variables.name: %ni_active_dhcp_gateway_v4
output_variables.description: Active Network DHCP Gateway (Router) IP Address v4

arguments.name: Device IDs/Names
arguments.description:
You can control multiple devices in a single action using Tasker's Pattern Matching.

For example, if you have a light called 'Ceiling 1' and another one called 'Ceiling 2', you can toggle them both by setting the name to 'Ceiling *'.

All options bellow will apply to all matching devices.

arguments.name: Names
arguments.description:
One or more comma or newline separated array names.

Don't use () at the end of their names, since that will join them together in a comma separated string.

arguments.name: Background Colour
arguments.description:
The background color of the whole widget.

If you don't specify text color, it'll automatically be chosen to contrast with this.

arguments.name: Texts
arguments.description:
Depending on the chosen layout, these texts can appear in different places:

- Buttons: are used as labels for each button
- Media: is used as the subtitle for the widget

arguments.name: Text Styles
arguments.description:
Styles for each of the texts above.

If you specify less styles than texts, the last specified style will be used for the remainder of the texts.

A style can be:

- a color in HTML notation or one of the color Material Design tokens (primary, onPrimary, secondary, etc) 
- a number to set the text size in sp
- one of 'sansserif', 'serif', 'monospace', 'cursive' to set the font family
- one of 'left', 'right', 'center', 'start', 'end' to set text alignment
-italic
-bold
-underline
-linethrough

For example, you could set 2 texts with 2 different styles:
- Red, bold text
- Green, italic, underlined text

by setting this to

#FF0000 bold,#00FF00 italic underline.

IMPORTANT: Keep in mind that the title also counts as a text, so the first style you provide is assigned to the title.

arguments.name: Images
arguments.description:
Depending on the chosen layout, these images can appear in different places:

- Buttons: are used as the main image for each button
- Media: the first image will be used as the main one on the left. The rest are used as buttons below.

arguments.name: Image Tints
arguments.description:
If you set this, you'll colorize the images above with a single, solid color.

You can specify an image not to be tinted by leaving the value empty.

If you specify less colors than images, the last specified colour will be used for the remainder of the images.

arguments.name: Image Sizes
arguments.description:
The size or sizes you want the images to have in dp (Density Independent Pixels).

If you specify less sizes than images, the last specified size will be used for the remainder of the images.

arguments.name: Tasks
arguments.description:
Tasks to be ran when you tap on the texts/images above.

Specify one task for each of the text/image, or leave blank to make them not clickable.

arguments.name: Commands
arguments.description:
Commands to be ran when you tap on the texts/images above.

Specify one command for each of the text/image, or leave blank to make them not clickable.

These commands will trigger the 'Command' event in Tasker. Check that for more info.

arguments.name: Command Prefix
arguments.description: If set, will prepend "prefix=:=" to all your commands above (where "prefix" is the actual prefix you specify here).

arguments.name: Custom Layout
arguments.description:
Specify your custom layout here as a JSON structure.

You can also directly use an HTTP/S URL or a file path here.

Make sure to escape any variables you are using inside JSON strings with the 'Variable Convert' action > 'JSON Encode' if needed.

Click below to learn all about Custom Layouts.

arguments.name: Material You Colors
arguments.description: If enabled, will use Material You colors whenever colors are not set explicitly above, which means, the Widget colors will match your wallpaper.

arguments.name: Number of Columns
arguments.description:
The number of columns the widget will have to show your data.

For example, if you specify 10 texts and set Number of Columns to 5, you'll get 2 rows with 5 columns each.

arguments.name: Ask To Add If Not Present
arguments.description: If the widget is not already added to your home screen, show a popup asking you to add it.

arguments.name: Separator
arguments.description: Character(s) used to separate the values in the multi-value fields (Texts, Images, Tasks, Commands, etc.). For example, set this to a semicolon so a comma can be used inside a value. Leave empty to separate on a comma.

arguments.name: Latitude
arguments.description: If left empty, will use current location.

arguments.name: Longitude
arguments.description: If left empty, will use current location.

arguments.name: Seconds Since Epoch
arguments.description: If left empty, will use current time.

arguments.name: Custom Sun Elevation Angle
arguments.description: Enter one or more sun elevation angles to find the two times they occur each day: once as the sun is rising (morning) and again as it is setting (evening).

arguments.name: Overwrite Source Variable
arguments.description: When on (the default), the formatted JSON is written straight back to the variable used in the JSON field above, so this action works as a simple passthrough without you having to use the %fj_formatted output. Has no effect if the JSON field isn't a single plain variable (for example, literal text or a structured reference like %var.key).

arguments.name: Variable Array
arguments.description: This field is a **String** and is **mandatory** and must NOT be empty. It should be the variable '%rows' or a more suitable name for the situation, if possible. The result rows of the query are stored in the specified array with a row at each index. The columns within each row are separated by the Output Column Divider, if needed.

arguments.name: Position
arguments.description: Is **mandatory** and **HAS** to be a value between 1 and 999999. This **MUST NOT** be left empty.
